Thank you for your review!  I have a 2024 i5 M60, and I am going to share my experiences with you.  

There are several features and equipment that we do not get in the U.S.  We tried to work with BMW US/NA and they were terrible to work with.  Very disappointed.    

Examples:

1)	We do not get M seat belts.  This is a piece of standard equipment for all i5 M60s everywhere else but in the U.S.  We tried to add it and even pay for it and they said no.  
2)	We do not get the Digital Rear 4-Zone Climate Control.  Again, everyone else gets it, but us in the U.S.  We tried to get it and even pay for it.  First, they said yes as a stand-alone option for $650 (crazy) and then they changed their mind and said no.  
3)	We do not get the Integral Active Steering.  Again, standard on all M60s, but in the U.S.  First, they said yes as a stand-alone option for $1,150 (crazy) and then they changed their mind and said no.  
4)	We cannot get comfort or multi-contour seats. They call them Luxury Seating Package.  So, in the U.S., we get manual headrests, manual leg extenders, and no other seat options.
5)	The panoramic glass roof is a joke.  It is a plain glass with no Sky Lounge LED lights.  We can’t open it at all.  I am glad to see 2024 Mercedes-Benz C, E, and S Classes have them and are fully operational.  
6)	The lower door panels and window switches are cheap plastic.  Kia has better-quality buttons. 
7)	No door sills.  Even the Honda Accord has illuminated door sills.
8)	No front seat massaging.
9)	No soft-close doors.


Keep in mind that some of the options mentioned above are available on the 530i, 530i xDrive, 540i xDrive, and 550e xDrive in other countries.  More and more, BMW US/NA is cheapening their product.  Worse, here in the U.S. we are treated worse than in other countries when it comes to standard features, options, and packages while they keep raising their prices.

After a while looking at the interior, you feel something is missing.  There is no door or cover to cover the cup holders.  The car looks cheap, unfinished, and not so luxurious.

I am also not fond of multiple-color seats.   I have seen BMW do a better job with other models.  I am not sure what happened with the 5 Series.  I miss Tartufo, Coffee, or just simple black.  What is up with grey and copper?  It doesn’t look good at all.  It appears that we are looking at some cheap car.       

As for the range.  It is awful.  If we have to watch how we drive, then that’s not an “M”60 car.  And it takes a very long time to fully charge the vehicle even with the Level II charger.

Anyone remember the electrical Ford Focus based on the petrol version? This one is more or less the same concept. Making an electric and combustion version on the same platform is insane in 2024. The range is low, the car is way too heavy,  it handles poorly and it’s insanely overpriced. There is no frunk either. What a turd.

Thank you for the great video with honest and precise details. I’ve had my speced up eDrive40 for about 3 months and got 6k on the clock. I did test drive many similar cars before I bought the i5 including Tesla, Taycan, BYD, Polestar etc but hands down this is much better car in terms of comforts, tech, specs etc. just love the dynamic dampers and 4 wheel steering. I have owned 2 consecutive previous 5 series models and this one has a pretty amazing and reliable driver assistance system including automatic lane change when you put the blinkers on and turn your head. The most remarkable thing is the level of accuracy and trust you can put on them. The driver fatigue monitoring system is just next level unlike previous generations. Just tried to trick it in a few different scenarios and it did just pick up when I was showing signs of actual tiredness. Also i5 is a bit bigger than the predecessor in terms of external and also interior dimensions. The rear seat leg and head room do feel bigger than the previous version as well. Compared to my 2021 M550i (literally the lite version of M5), i5 does feel quite underpowered but compared to many other similarly priced electric and ICE cars, i5 has more than enough power and agility that you will mostly be the first to get off green lights. And the RWD with very responsive electric motor does make it so lively and fun to drive and you can put your back out secretly, without anyone hearing a raging engine if you really want. Overall, the i5 eDrive40 is a very practical, comfortable and fun to drive car that you can spend hours in without getting bored. Plus you get 5 year free charging, servicing and 8 year free roadside. Cheers.

While @OneTireFire provides a fairly good review, I offer a few observations as it may help evaluating this model. I know I looked at countless reviews while shopping!

In no particular order:
- The boot (trunk) fits normal-sized interior doors (for Europe ) lying flat, but of course with the front seats pulled up to an uncomfortable - but still drivable - seating position. 
-  I've seen reviews of the USA version G60, and that lower space in the boot is filled with a donut spare tire, so there's no indentation in the floor. 
- The parking cameras and auto park function help me quite a bit when it's tight. The auto park/unpark function controls the steering wheel and the driver controls the pedals. It takes some getting used to, but for backing out of long, tight spots I've appreciate it. I don't see the point of for the optional RWS unless you want to spend more money.
- Controls - like turning off the beeping when over the speed limit @15:53 in the video - can be assigned hand-motion shortcuts... which was one of the first things I did.
- There are some functions, like seat adjustment, ambient lighting, etc., that are programmed into your personal setting. My wife has a key, I have the other: the car knows the set up when that key is present. Other functions, like the climate controls, need time to figure out. But no need to touch the screen. Especially when driving, the iDrive wheel and other controls on the middle console and on the steering wheel can be used instead. Maybe not for the climate control, but I've just kept that on Auto. The (hidden) vents are manually controlled, as @OneTireFire noted.
- I like the steering wheel! It's comfortable and goes well with the rest of the car.
- The HUD is very well done. When navigation is in use, it provides (written) directions so the voice directions can be turned off (for example, if passengers are sleeping.) It also helps the driver keep the car in the middle of the driving lane.  In the video, see when @OneTireFire is driving through the narrow road @11:27-11:51 for this in action. 
- When you turn off the engine, the seat goes back and the steering wheel up, which provides additional room to get exit the car. Starting the car reverses that.
- The cell phone key function works fine, as does the app to check the status of the car. There's a valet card key but I haven't used that yet.
- In the video those tablet attach points on the back of the front seats @4:44, and the sunshades must be optional since I don't have them either. Why someone would get sunshades with tinted windows is beyond me! I don't have nets on the backs either. Nets were never used on my old E36 and just add clutter. I don't have the pana roof or sunroof options either. But I saw somewhere the reason the pana roof's sunshade goes in that direction is the passengers get more headroom.
- The vents in the bottom half of the grill open when at operating temps, as needed, to cool the motor.

Sorry this is so long, but maybe these observations will help someone in their car shopping!

I ended up going with mocha "veganza" because I was not confident I would like the copper brown/atlas gray genuine leather option. I did not get the extended shadow line package for one reason and it turned out to be inaccurate. I did NOT want to drive around with a permanently illuminated kidney grille for my lifetime with the vehicle. So, I didn't option the extended shadow line despite otherwise thinking it improved the styling of the 5er. HOWEVER there is an option to disable the grille illumination in iDrive OS. If I decide to lease return this vehicle, I will probably spec a model with extended shadow line next time.

I own a 2024 i5 M60, my third 5 Series, and after 17 months of driving, I regret to say I wouldn't choose an i5 again. The car's heavy weight causes frequent tire issues; even minor road imperfections can result in bubbled or torn tires. I've experienced a cracked wheel and a bent tire on the freeway. Despite having Wheel and Tire coverage, I've had to replace eight tires in 17 months, and the coverage doesn't include dented tires that still connect to the wheel...I have become the most paranoid -of-potholes driver and still, due to weight, tires bubble and wheels dent with the smallest of bumps!!!  The braking system is unreliable unless used in ReGen brake mode. I even use ReGen on the freeway because the car brakes very slowly. Remarkably, there was a brake module recall three months after purchase, but BMW took over nine months for the repair/replacement. My initial complaints about the car's weight and electric nature were dismissed by BMW, telling me to "get accustomed" to it. This is the most unreliable braking experience I've had with a BMW.  Best part of this car is the steering...excellent radius and very light.

Additionally, the perforated seats are prone to getting dirty and require detailed cleaning. The car's lack of aerodynamics results in significant drag, with a range of only 230 miles at best, despite a stated range of 250 miles. The front spoiler is also prone to catching debris due to its low position. The AC system, which seems common to all 5 Series models, fails to cool effectively unless set to maximum. Overall, my experience with this car has been disappointing, and BMW's lack of response to these issues discourages me from choosing another BMW in the future. Don't let the good looks deceive you.  For $116,000 (fully loaded with EVERYTHING), you're better off buying the M5 Hybrid or another electric car all together, like a Porsche Macan Electric.

Operating touchscreens or smooth touch surfaces in a car is extremely distracting and massively increases the risk of accidents. 
This is"blind driving": You can feel physical buttons. You know exactly where they are without taking your eyes off the road.

No feedback: Touch buttons often lack clear confirmation that the command has been recognized.
